doc.title: Vince DiMartino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 8, 2025

title: Music is sound not sight: solfeggio, conductors and the Hindemith Sonata
summary: He argues notation is a shortcut, criticizes conductors who only teach rehearsing, and describes learning phrasing from string bowings.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Yeah. So basically there is no — okay let me show you. Okay. Follow this music and I can’t find a piece of music, all right? Okay. So okay. You here?

It’s music — if you’re looking for music to make sound, all you do is you crumble it up and put it in your fireplace and you can hear it burn. Really. ‘Cause it doesn’t exist. This is a shortcut for people to play together or to practice certain things that people think are important. And that’s all. Otherwise it’d be like, “Okay, we’re going to play Beethoven Fifth. Okay? But he said it a hundred times already. You see? And when I work with a conductor that doesn’t bring that out, they’re not good. That’s so simple. See they’ve been taught by somebody who didn’t teach them music. They taught them how to rehearse. How to get people to play together.
